newsitem.title: USA: Phelps Dodge says earnings off 46 percent.
newsitem.headline: Phelps Dodge says earnings off 46 percent.

text.p: Phelps Dodge Corp. said Thursday its earnings slumped 46 percent in the latest quarter, blaming the downturn on a drop in copper prices.
The world's largest copper producer reported net income of $102.2 million, or $1.57 a share, in the fourth quarter of 1996, down from year-earlier earnings of $190.0 million, or $2.73 a share.
Sales fell to $970.6 million from $1.05 billion.
"The copper market, a significant factor in our performance, again surprised many observers," said Douglas Yearley, chairman and chief executive officer.

"World consumption remained robust and was, from many indications, again at record levels," he said. "Prices, although lower and plagued with unusual volatility, proved more resistant to downside pressures than many had anticipated."
The price of copper averaged 99 cents a pound in the fourth quarter, compared with $1.32 a year earlier.
Phelps Dodge said its mine output totalled 197,100 tons in the fourth quarter, down from 199,700 tons a year earlier.
Phelps Dodge's stock was up $1 at $72.625 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
